jobs.title: 3D Environment Artist & Level Designer
jobs.description: 3D Environment Artist & Level Designer ScapeWorld Entertainment · Remote Level: Senior to lead Location: Remote, CET overlap Contract: Full time, long term About us We are ScapeWorld Entertainment, a fully remote Swedish game studio of just over 20 people. We are building Scape, a platform of multiplayer games where a player’s identity carries across all of them. We have just launched our first game within Scape. Our senior team has shipped and run live games at studios including Arrowhead (Helldivers 2), Avalanche Studios and Ubisoft. The project Our next game is a cleaning and restoration sim set in a shared neighbourhood. Every player has a place of their own that starts buried in junk and grime, and puts it in order in full view of neighbours who are doing the same. Cleaning games are usually played alone or in short co-op sessions. We want to make one set in a neighbourhood that players share and keep coming back to, and we want to do it well. We have a working prototype and are refining the loop now. If you play games like this and have views on what makes them satisfying, you will enjoy this. About the role We are looking for a senior to lead 3D environment artist who is also a level designer. You will be the only level designer on the project. You own the game’s spaces, from first layout through to dressed and lit, and you are responsible for delivering them. The role is split roughly evenly between environment art, mostly props and other environment 3D assets, and level design, which includes some gameplay design. On the design side you work with our Creative Director and engineering, and you bring your level and gameplay design experience into those discussions. On the art side you work with the rest of the art team. You report to the Art Director. What you will do Environment art Model and texture props and other environment 3D assets. As a Senior Optical Design Engineer, you will own optical designs from concept through lab validation, turning requirements into lens designs and optical assemblies that perform reliably in the real world. This position is central to our mission of delivering cutting-edge free-space optical systems for space applications, and it will support successful pre-production runs and strong collaboration with our suppliers. This position reports to our Responsible Engineer, Optical Systems, and is based in our Toulouse, France office. Our working language is English. What you will be doing Design and optimize lenses and optical systems, from first-order layout to detailed optimization with ray tracing and physical optics propagation (POP). Carry out tolerance analysis and Monte Carlo simulations to predict manufacturing and assembly yield, and define realistic tolerances with suppliers. jobs.title: Langfuse - Product Designer
jobs.description: Why Design at Langfuse Your work will shape how engineers build with AI. Langfuse is often the primary interface engineers use to debug, evaluate, and improve their LLM applications. The designs you ship will be used for hours each day by thousands of developers and non-developers. They'll tell you about it in GitHub issues, on X, and in our community Slack channels. Everything we build is open source (MIT-licensed) and immediately visible. The design challenges here are genuinely hard. You're designing for technical users and business users alike who care about information density, speed, and precision. Traces contain dozens of nested LLM calls with massive prompts and completions. Users need to set up evaluators, manage prompt versions, configure integrations, and build monitoring dashboards before they even start analyzing results. You need to make both the setup and the daily use feel intuitive and easy. You will also have direct exposure to how cutting-edge LLM applications are built. Deeply understanding the problems our users solve will make you a better designer and along the way makes you an expert on LLM engineering yourself. You will grow at Langfuse by Owning our product design end-to-end. You'll be the first dedicated designer at Langfuse. Today, our engineers design as they build, which has gotten us far, but we need someone who can elevate the entire experience. You'll own the design system, and visual language across the product. You'll set the standard for how Langfuse looks and feels. Making data-dense interfaces intuitive. Langfuse surfaces traces, scores, costs, latencies, token counts, prompt versions, and evaluation results. You'll figure out how to present complex, nested data in ways that help engineers find what they need fast. Simplifying complex workflows. jobs.description: We’re looking for a UI designer who loves casual games. You know what makes a game feel intuitive and fun to play, and you can turn that into clean, good-looking UI. You’ll be assisting the SOHO Art team and reporting directly to our Game Art Lead. Heads up: we’ll ask you to do a short graphics assignment as part of the process. What you’ll be doing: Creating UI assets - designing visually appealing interfaces that align with the game’s art direction. Matching our style - we have a very specific look. You’ll study it and create new elements that feel like part of the same family, so everything fits right in next to what we already have. Using AI tools - speeding up your work with AI: quick ideas, variations, and rough explorations. Then you polish the final assets by hand until they meet our quality bar. Helping out with general art - characters, backgrounds, props, and other 2D assets when needed. Taking feedback and running with it - we iterate a lot, and quick, smooth revisions make everyone’s life easier. Owning your work - you decide how to scope it, prioritise it, and deliver it, without needing someone to hold your hand. What we’re looking for: Experience working on casual games. Strong UI design and execution skills, with good UX instincts. Excellent 2D art skills. Strong portfolio showcasing high-quality UI art for mobile titles from concept to final in-game execution. The ability to work independently and figure out unclear problems, while taking on board feedback from the Game Art Lead. Good English so that you can explain your design decisions clearly to people from different teams. Solid skills in standard design tools like Figma and Photoshop (or similar). Comfort in a small team, where you’ll wear a few hats and switch between big-picture thinking and hands-on work. Nice to have: Any UI animation skills. Passion for games and player psychology.
